proofs.proof_tex:
Set
\[
p=\frac{k+1}{k+m+1},
\qquad
q=\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)}.
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:localized\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\), applied to the family whose membership is certified by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}family\text{-}membership}\), gives constants \(c>0\) and \(\varepsilon_0>0\) such that
\[
\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\geq c\varepsilon^p,
\qquad 0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0.
\tag{1}
\]
For an arbitrary pair in the same class with \(D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq\varepsilon\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:full\text{-}law\text{-}residual\text{-}reduction}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:scalar\text{-}finite\text{-}type\text{-}weak\text{-}rigidity}\) give, in this order,
\[
\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
\leq C_0D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
\leq C_0\varepsilon
\]
and
\[
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
\leq C_1\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^q
\leq C_1C_0^q\varepsilon^q.
\tag{2}
\]
Taking the supremum over the set in Definition \(\mathrm{def:inverse\text{-}modulus}\) proves the upper inequality.  Combining it with (1) proves the displayed bracket.

For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), direct substitution gives
\[
p=\frac{3}{4},
\qquad
q=\frac{2}{(2+1)(1+1)}=\frac13.
\]
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:primary\text{-}morse\text{-}audit}\) supplies the lower family inside the stated primary class, so the specialized bracket follows.  Finally (2) with \(D_H=0\) gives \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}=0\) for every zero-law pair.  Taking the supremum over those pairs yields \(\Omega_{k,m}(0)=0\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:representation\text{-}distance}\), this is precisely recovery up to the common permutation and the coordinatewise circle-diffeomorphism action.

The specialization \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\) in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}full\text{-}modulus}\) gives
\[
c\varepsilon^{3/4}
\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)
\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}.
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:radial\text{-}subclass\text{-}frontier}\) independently gives
\[
\Omega_{2,1}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)
\asymp\varepsilon^{(2+1)/(2+1+1)}
=\varepsilon^{3/4}.
\]
The equality \(\Omega_{2,1}(0)=0\) from Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}full\text{-}modulus}\), together with Definitions \(\mathrm{def:inverse\text{-}modulus}\) and \(\mathrm{def:representation\text{-}distance}\), proves the zero-law quotient-recovery assertion.

For completeness, suppose that some scalar contrast \(r_{\theta i}\) were constant on a nonempty open arc \(I\).  Then \(r_{\theta i}'(t)=0\) for every \(t\in I\), so Definition of \(Z_{\theta i}\) gives \(I\subseteq Z_{\theta i}\).  This contradicts Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:critical\text{-}cardinality}\), which requires \(|Z_{\theta i}|\leq J<\infty\).  Equivalently, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}profile}\) gives a strictly positive lower bound at every point outside the finite set.  Thus plateau rotations lie outside the stated class.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:certified\text{-}spectral\text{-}law\text{-}recovery}\) states that, for every \(M>0\),
\[
\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}}
\Pr_\theta\!\left\{
\frac{D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)}{\rho_N}>M
\right\}=0.
\tag{1}
\]
This is exactly the first asserted uniform stochastic order.  Put
\[
q=\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)}.
\]
Because \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}=k-1>0\), Definition of \(\rho_N\) gives \(\rho_N\to0\).  Both \(\theta\) and \(\widehat\theta_N\) belong to the model class by Definition \(\mathrm{def:certified\text{-}spectral\text{-}estimator}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:full\text{-}law\text{-}residual\text{-}reduction}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:scalar\text{-}finite\text{-}type\text{-}weak\text{-}rigidity}\) therefore imply, whenever the law discrepancy is below a fixed small-radius threshold,
\[
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
\leq C D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)^q.
\tag{2}
\]
For every \(M\geq1\), on the event \(D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)\leq M\rho_N\), equation (2) gives
\[
\frac{d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)}{\rho_N^q}
\leq C M^q
\]
for all sufficiently large \(N\).  The complement has uniformly vanishing tail after first taking \(N\to\infty\) and then \(M\to\infty\), by (1).  This proves the second asserted uniform stochastic order.

In the primary case, \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}=1\) and \(n=2\), so
\[
\rho_N=(N/\log N)^{-1/(2+2)}=(N/\log N)^{-1/4}.
\]
Here \(q=1/3\), and hence
\[
\rho_N^q=(N/\log N)^{-1/12},
\]
which proves the last assertion.

The coverage display is exactly Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:corrected\text{-}confidence\text{-}coverage}\), so it remains to bound the diameter.  Put
\[
r_N=2c_\alpha\rho_N+2\delta_N.
\]
Let \(\vartheta\) and \(\vartheta'\) be any two representing models in the displayed supremum.  The complete-family distance is the quotient of the Euclidean product of the component Hellinger metrics by the finite common-permutation action.  To verify its triangle inequality directly, choose minimizing permutations for \((\vartheta,\widehat\theta_N)\) and \((\widehat\theta_N,\vartheta')\), compose them, and apply Minkowski's inequality to the vector of square-root-density differences in all environments.  The composed permutation is admissible for \((\vartheta,\vartheta')\); hence Definition \(\mathrm{def:full\text{-}law\text{-}distance}\) gives
\[
D_H(\vartheta,\vartheta')
\leq D_H(\vartheta,\widehat\theta_N)
+D_H(\widehat\theta_N,\vartheta')
\leq2r_N
=4c_\alpha\rho_N+4\delta_N.
\tag{1}
\]
Since \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), the right side of (1) is \(O(\rho_N)\) and tends to zero.  With
\[
q=\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)},
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:full\text{-}law\text{-}residual\text{-}reduction}\) followed by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:scalar\text{-}finite\text{-}type\text{-}weak\text{-}rigidity}\) applies uniformly to every such pair and yields
\[
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\vartheta,\vartheta')
\leq C\{4c_\alpha\rho_N+4\delta_N\}^q
=O(\rho_N^q).
\tag{2}
\]
The bound in (2) is simultaneous over all representing pairs in the set, so taking the supremum proves the asserted diameter order (indeed, the order bound is deterministic once \(c_\alpha\) is fixed).  For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), one has \(q=1/3\) and \(\rho_N=(N/\log N)^{-1/4}\), giving \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a class-uniform constant \(C<\infty\) such that every aligned pair \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) with \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq1\) satisfies
\[
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
\leq C\,\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^q,
\qquad
q=\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)}.
\]
This estimate uses only the scalar ratio residuals; it does not assert the sharper incompressible exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Relabel the coordinates of \(\widetilde\theta\) by the group permutation fixed in Definition \(\mathrm{def:analytic\text{-}residual}\).  This is allowed by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}grouping}\), and after this relabeling the optimizing permutation is the identity.

We first record uniform consequences of membership in Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).  By Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:causal\text{-}factorization}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:perfect\text{-}intervention\text{-}family}\), reverse integration in a topological ordering of the intervened DAG gives
\[
q_i^e(t)=\int_{\mathbb T^{n-1}}p_\theta^{i,e}(t,x_{-i})\,d\lambda^{n-1}(x_{-i}).
\]
Indeed, each nonintervened conditional density integrates to one when a terminal nonintervened vertex is removed, and iteration leaves only \(q_i^e(t)\).  Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:density\text{-}bounds}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:density\text{-}smoothness}\) therefore imply, by differentiation under this finite compact integral,
\[
c_0\leq q_i^e(t)\leq C_0,
\qquad
\lVert q_i^e\rVert_{C^k(\mathbb T)}\leq K.
\tag{1}
\]
The same bounds hold for the corresponding mechanisms of \(\widetilde\theta\).  It follows from (1), the chain rule, and Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}smoothness}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}conditioning}\) that the baseline gauges and their inverses, the maps \(F_\theta,F_{\widetilde\theta}\), and the transition map
\[
T=F_\theta^{-1}\circ F_{\widetilde\theta}
\]
have class-uniform \(C^k\) bounds.  Moreover, there are class-uniform constants \(0<b\leq B<\infty\) such that
\[
b\leq \sigma_{\min}\{DT(z)\}
\leq \sigma_{\max}\{DT(z)\}\leq B
\qquad(z\in\mathbb T^n).
\tag{2}
\]
The gauged profiles \(R_i=r_{\theta i}\circ\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\) and \(S_i=r_{\widetilde\theta i}\circ\beta_{\widetilde\theta i}^{-1}\) also have class-uniform \(C^k\) norms.  Because (1) makes every \(\beta_{\theta i}\) uniformly bi-Lipschitz, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}profile}\) becomes
\[
|R_i'(u)|\geq a\,\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}(u,\mathcal Z_i)^m,
\qquad
\mathcal Z_i=\beta_{\theta i}(Z_{\theta i}),
\qquad
|\mathcal Z_i|\leq J,
\tag{3}
\]
for a class-uniform \(a>0\), where the cardinality bound is Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:critical\text{-}cardinality}\).

Put
\[
E=\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta),
\qquad
e_i(z)=R_i\{T_i(z)\}-S_i(z_i).
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def:analytic\text{-}residual}\) and the preceding uniform bounds give
\[
\lVert e_i\rVert_{L^2(\lambda^n)}\leq E,
\qquad
\lVert e_i\rVert_{C^k(\mathbb T^n)}\leq B_1
\tag{4}
\]
with a class-uniform \(B_1\).

We next derive the interpolation estimate needed below.  Choose a compactly supported smooth signed approximation kernel \(A\) of integral one whose moments of orders one through \(k-1\) vanish, and periodize its rescaling \(A_h(x)=h^{-n}A(x/h)\) for \(0<h<h_0\).  Such a kernel is obtained from a finite linear combination of distinct rescalings of one smooth bump by solving the finite Vandermonde system for the required moments.  Cauchy--Schwarz and Taylor's formula with integral remainder give, for every periodic \(C^k\) function \(g\),
\[
\lVert A_h*g\rVert_\infty
\leq \lVert A_h\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2
\leq C h^{-n/2}\lVert g\rVert_2,
\]
and
\[
\lVert g-A_h*g\rVert_\infty
\leq C h^k\lVert g\rVert_{C^k}.
\]
Applying these inequalities to (4), and taking \(h=E^{1/(k+n/2)}\) when \(E\) is sufficiently small, yields
\[
\lVert e_i\rVert_\infty
\leq C\{E h^{-n/2}+h^k\}
\leq C E^a,
\qquad
a=\frac{k}{k+n/2}.
\tag{5}
\]
For the remaining bounded range of \(E\leq1\), increasing \(C\) makes (5) valid as well.  Write \(\eta=CE^a\).

We now turn (3) into a scalar oscillation bound.  Let \(I\subset\mathbb T\) be an arc of length \(\ell\leq\pi\).  Removing at most \(J\) points of \(\mathcal Z_i\) leaves a component of length at least \(\ell/(J+1)\).  On the middle half of that component, the distance from \(\mathcal Z_i\) is at least \(\ell/\{4(J+1)\}\).  The derivative \(R_i'\) has a constant sign on the component, since its zero set is \(\mathcal Z_i\).  Integration of (3) on the middle half therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{osc}_{I}R_i
\geq c\ell^{m+1}.
\tag{6}
\]
The same argument on any fixed arc of length \(\pi\) also gives a fixed positive oscillation.

For fixed \(z_i\), the image
\[
I_{i,z_i}=\{T_i(z_i,z_{-i}):z_{-i}\in\mathbb T^{n-1}\}
\]
is connected because \(n\geq2\) and \(\mathbb T^{n-1}\) is connected.  Equation (5), with \(S_i(z_i)\) fixed on this fiber, gives
\[
\operatorname{osc}_{I_{i,z_i}}R_i\leq2\eta.
\tag{7}
\]
For sufficiently small \(E\), the fixed-arc consequence of (6) excludes the possibility that \(I_{i,z_i}\) is the whole circle or contains an arc of length \(\pi\).  Thus it is contained in an arc of length at most \(\pi\), and (6)--(7) imply the uniform transverse-fiber bound
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{\mathbb T} I_{i,z_i}
\leq C\eta^{1/(m+1)}=:\delta.
\tag{8}
\]

We construct an admissible coordinate gauge from (8).  Let \(A_T\in\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb Z)\) be the homology matrix of the torus diffeomorphism \(T\).  If \(j\ne i\) and \((A_T)_{ij}\ne0\), the restriction of \(T_i\) to a transverse \(z_j\)-circle has nonzero degree and is therefore onto \(\mathbb T\), contradicting (8) for \(\delta<\pi\).  Hence \(A_T\) is diagonal.  Since it is an invertible integer matrix, every diagonal entry \(d_i=(A_T)_{ii}\) belongs to \(\{-1,1\}\).  Choose a lift
\[
\overline T_i(z)=d_i z_i+u_i(z),
\]
where \(u_i\) is \(2\pi\)-periodic in every variable, and define
\[
\overline\phi_i(t)=d_i t+int_{\mathbb T^{n-1}}u_i(t,z_{-i})\,d\lambda^{n-1}(z_{-i}).
\tag{9}
\]
The short-arc lift furnished by (8) shows directly from (9) that
\[
\sup_z|\overline T_i(z)-\overline\phi_i(z_i)|\leq C\delta.
\tag{10}
\]

It remains to check that \(\phi_i=\overline\phi_i\pmod{2\pi}\) is a circle diffeomorphism.  If a one-variable \(C^2\) function \(g\) has oscillation at most \(\delta\) and \(\lVert g''\rVert_\infty\leq B\), Taylor's formula gives, for \(0<s<1\),
\[
|g'(t)|\leq \frac{2\delta}{s}+\frac{B s}{2}.
\]
Taking \(s\) proportional to \(\delta^{1/2}\) proves \(\lVert g'\rVert_\infty\leq C\delta^{1/2}\).  Apply this to every transverse restriction in (8).  Then
\[
\max_{j\ne i}\lVert\partial_jT_i\rVert_\infty\leq C\delta^{1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
By (2), the Euclidean norm of row \(i\) of \(DT\) is at least \(b\).  Equations (2) and (11) consequently imply, once \(E\) is sufficiently small,
\[
|\partial_iT_i(z)|\geq b/2.
\tag{12}
\]
The continuous function \(\partial_iT_i\) has one sign on the connected torus.  Differentiating (9), averaging (12), and using (2) show that \(\phi_i\) has degree \(d_i\) and
\[
b/2\leq|\phi_i'(t)|\leq B.
\tag{13}
\]
Thus \(\phi_i\in\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb T)\), and both \(\phi_i\) and \(\phi_i^{-1}\) are uniformly Lipschitz.  Equations (10) and (13) also imply
\[
\sup_x\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}
\{(T^{-1})_i(x),\phi_i^{-1}(x_i)\}
\leq C\delta.
\tag{14}
\]
Indeed, for \(x=T(z)\), the left side is at most the inverse Lipschitz constant in (13) times \(\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}\{T_i(z),\phi_i(z_i)\}\).

Finally define the coordinate reparameterization between the original latent gauges by
\[
\varphi_i=\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\circ\phi_i\circ\beta_{\widetilde\theta i}.
\tag{15}
\]
All complete latent densities, all decoder Jacobians, and all baseline-gauge derivatives are bounded above and below by the class constants.  Hence changes of variables through \(F_\theta\) or \(F_{\widetilde\theta}\) compare either mixture measure in Definition \(\mathrm{def:representation\text{-}distance}\) with \(\lambda^n\) by fixed factors.  Equations (10), (14), and (15) therefore give, for the same alignment and its algebraic inverse,
\[
L_{\theta\leftarrow\widetilde\theta}(\mathrm{id},\varphi)
+L_{\widetilde\theta\leftarrow\theta}(\mathrm{id},\varphi)
\leq C\delta
\leq C E^{a/(m+1)}.
\]
Taking the infimum in Definition \(\mathrm{def:representation\text{-}distance}\) and using \(a/(m+1)=k/\{(k+n/2)(m+1)\}\) proves the claim.  Enlarging \(C\) handles the bounded range of \(E\) not covered by the smallness choices, because Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:symmetric\text{-}quotient\text{-}pseudometric}\) gives \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\leq\pi\sqrt n\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every fixed bounded class \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) containing the lower family of Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}family\text{-}membership}\), there are constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)
\leq C\varepsilon^{,k/\{(k+n/2)(m+1)\}}.
\]
In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse class containing the audited family this reads \(c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}\).  Moreover \(\Omega_{k,m}(0)=0\), so equality of the complete observed-law families identifies the encoder up to one node permutation and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms.  No sharp full-class upper exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The claimed sharp full-class upper bound requires the unresolved arbitrary-diffeomorphism incompressible-rigidity estimate. The proposed claim retains the proved sharp lower bound and adds the strongest full-class upper bound derivable from the frozen scalar finite-type ratios by interpolation, without substituting the radial subclass for the full class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
When \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\), every primary Morse class containing the audited family satisfies
\[
c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}
\]
for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), whereas the radial restriction satisfies \(\Omega_{2,1}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{3/4}\).  At \(\varepsilon=0\), the full class has componentwise circular recovery up to one node permutation.  A contrast with a nonempty plateau is excluded by the finite-cardinality and finite-type assumptions.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The full primary Morse class has a proved three-quarters lower exponent and a proved one-third upper exponent, while three-quarters is two-sided only on the radial restriction. Claiming the full-class three-quarters equality would still assume the unresolved rigidity step.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under independent environment sampling and certified tolerance \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), the positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator satisfies, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\),
\[
D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N),
\qquad
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\rho_N^{,k/\{(k+n/2)(m+1)\}}\right).
\]
In the primary case \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\), the law rate is \((N/\log N)^{-1/4}\) and the certified full-class representation rate is \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The law estimator is uniformly certified at radius rho, but the three-quarters inverse exponent is not proved on the full model class. The proved weak full-class modulus propagates instead to exponent k divided by ((k+n/2)(m+1)), giving the honest primary rate one-twelfth.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every fixed known \((k,m)\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the inverted set is uniformly honest,
\[
\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}}
\Pr_\theta\{[h_\theta]\in\mathcal C_N(\alpha)\}
\geq1-\alpha-o(1).
\]
Its representing-model diameter
\[
\sup\left\{d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\vartheta,\vartheta'):
\vartheta,\vartheta'\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m},\
D_H(\vartheta,\widehat\theta_N)\vee
D_H(\vartheta',\widehat\theta_N)
\leq2c_\alpha\rho_N+2\delta_N\right\}
\]
is \(O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\rho_N^{,k/\{(k+n/2)(m+1)\}}\right)\).  In the primary case this diameter is \(O_{\mathbb P}\{(N/\log N)^{-1/12}\}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Uniform coverage is proved, but the originally asserted sharp representation diameter requires the unresolved full-class modulus. The law-space triangle inequality combined with the proved weak full-class modulus gives the displayed slower, fully justified diameter.

proposed.statement:
For every fixed bounded class \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) containing the lower family of Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}family\text{-}membership}\), there are constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)
\leq C\varepsilon^{,k/\{(k+n/2)(m+1)\}}.
\]
In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse class containing the audited family this reads \(c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}\).  Moreover \(\Omega_{k,m}(0)=0\), so equality of the complete observed-law families identifies the encoder up to one node permutation and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms.  No sharp full-class upper exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) is asserted.
proposed.justification: The theorem gives an explicit two-sided full-class modulus bracket, isolates the unresolved sharp upper exponent, and records the directly audited primary Morse specialization.
proposed.gap: Existing exact-identification results provide no nonzero-error exponent; the sharper three-quarters full-class upper remains the separate incompressible-rigidity question.
proposed.consumer: Likelihood and score-based causal representation learners obtain a rigorous, if conservative, translation from population law error to encoder error.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Rewire the narrowed theorem from the unresolved sharp-rigidity question to the proved weak scalar finite-type rigidity lemma and the established lower construction.

proposed.statement:
When \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\), every primary Morse class containing the audited family satisfies
\[
c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}
\]
for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), whereas the radial restriction satisfies \(\Omega_{2,1}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{3/4}\). A contrast with a nonempty plateau is excluded by the finite-cardinality and finite-type assumptions.
proposed.justification: The reduction separates the proved full-class bracket from the sharp radial three-quarters result and retains the exact-law sanity check.
proposed.gap: The exact papers have no stability rate, and the remaining gap is specifically between the full-class one-third upper and three-quarters lower exponents.
proposed.consumer: Two-angle systems receive a certified conservative full-class exponent, a sharp radial exponent, and a clear plateau boundary.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add the radial modulus symbol and dependency, remove reliance on an unproved sharp full-class equality, and wire the proposition to the narrowed full-class theorem.

proposed.statement:
Under independent environment sampling and certified tolerance \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), the positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator satisfies, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\),
\[
D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N),
\qquad
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\rho_N^{,k/\{(k+n/2)(m+1)\}}\right).
\]
In the primary case \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\), the law rate is \((N/\log N)^{-1/4}\) and the certified full-class representation rate is \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\).
proposed.justification: The computable estimator turns the proved conservative full-class population modulus into a usable finite-sample representation guarantee without numerical differentiation at critical points.
proposed.gap: No cited nonlinear causal-representation result supplies a full-class Hellinger-to-quotient rate; the sharper statistical exponent remains conditional on the open sharp rigidity problem.
proposed.consumer: Implementations on periodic latent coordinates obtain a certified stopping rule and an honest conservative representation radius from environment samples.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the unsupported sharp inverse-rate dependency by the proved narrowed full-class modulus while retaining the established spectral law estimator.

For every fixed known \((k,m)\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the inverted set is uniformly honest,
\[

\geq1-\alpha-o(1).
\]
Its representing-model diameter

proposed.gap: The sharp order-specific diameter remains open because it is equivalent to the missing sharp full-class inverse-modulus upper bound.
proposed.consumer: Users can report honest uncertainty for recovered circular factors with a conservative certified diameter.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Retain the proved coverage result and rewire the diameter proof to the narrowed full-class modulus; the estimator theorem is not needed for this direct inversion argument.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\le\varepsilon}d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\), with the proved full-class bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\le\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{k/\{(k+n/2)(m+1)\}}\) on each fixed bounded class containing the lower family, and the proved identity \(\Omega_{k,m}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\); the matching sharp full-class upper bound remains the open question \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimand functional must record the newly proved conservative full-class upper bound while continuing to distinguish it from the open sharp exponent and the solved radial identity.
